finding.claim: GET /rss passes the unvalidated user-supplied query parameter u directly to URI.open, causing the server to fetch an attacker-chosen URL and return the first 400 bytes of the response (full-read SSRF, including internal hosts and cloud metadata).
finding.source: params[:u], the 'u' query parameter of GET /rss (app.rb:7)

trace.note: get "/rss" route handler receives the request; params[:u] is attacker-controlled
params[:u] passed directly to URI.open, which issues the outbound HTTP(S) request
.read pulls the full response body from the attacker-chosen target
data[0, 400] returns the first 400 bytes of the response to the client

finding.guards_checked: None on the path: no scheme restriction, no host allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, no port restriction, no DNS or redirect re-validation. open-uri follows redirects only between http and https, which does not limit the initial target. Side note (unverified): on older Ruby versions URI.open can fall back to Kernel#open for non-URL strings, which may open local files or pipes; this is not SSRF but is on the same line.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only validation in app.rb is the TRUSTED host check at app.rb:13-14, which applies only to the /trusted route, not /rss. There is no before filter or helper in the 21-line file.
verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes params[:u] straight to URI.open(...).read, and params[:u] is attacker-controlled from the query string on GET /rss (app.rb:7); the host allowlist at app.rb:14 guards only /trusted, so the SSRF is unguarded and the first 400 bytes are returned at app.rb:9.
